title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Choppy tech break as Nvidia leadership reports roil the lineup
conditions.summary: Nasdaq futures are lower after reports that Nvidia's board is weighing CEO Jensen Huang's future, while Dow futures hold near flat. Yields sit near 5% after Wednesday's hotter-than-expected inflation data.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are down about 0.3% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.7% as of roughly 5 AM CT; Dow futures are up about 0.1% and Russell 2000 futures are flat.
Wednesday's close was strong: S&P 500 up 1.3% to 7,619, Nasdaq Composite up 1.6%, Dow up 0.5%, led by chip stocks after CoreWeave's results.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.99%, and the dollar index is flat around 102.8.
WTI crude is down about 0.5% near $86, gold is off about 0.9%, and bitcoin is down about 1% near $74,000.
The VIX is ticking up to around 18 after falling 10% on Wednesday.
Asia was mostly lower, with the Hang Seng down 1.3% and the Nikkei down 0.7%; chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix slipped.
Europe is higher, with the STOXX 600 up 0.5% and the DAX up 0.9%, helped by strong results from Adecco and Siemens.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: Weekly jobless claims are due at 7:30 AM CT; the prior week was 189,000. A consensus figure was not available in our sources.
October existing home sales and weekly oil inventories are also on today's calendar.
Fed speakers include Hammack, Goolsbee, Daly, Williams and Barr; markets are listening for any openness to a larger December rate hike after Wednesday's hot inflation report.
Money markets still see only outside odds of a 50 basis point December move, according to Newsquawk.
October producer prices (PPI) come out Friday.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Sonos beat on earnings and revenue for its fiscal fourth quarter; shares rose about 13% after hours.
Mercury Systems beat estimates with adjusted EPS of $0.52 versus $0.28 expected; shares rose about 13%.
ICL Group missed on earnings; shares fell about 2%.
Nebius is due to report today; its shares jumped more than 15% Wednesday after CoreWeave raised its outlook.
Applied Materials reports after today's close, and Cisco also reports today; both are key reads on AI and chip spending.
Also on today's calendar: Brookfield, Nu Holdings, Cerebras, QXO, Dillard's and Intuitive Machines.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): -5.5% — reports say the board is weighing CEO Jensen Huang's future over allegations about his personal conduct; nothing has been confirmed by the company.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): +4% — seen by traders as a relative winner amid Nvidia's leadership uncertainty.
AVGO (Broadcom): +3.6% — also bid as an alternative AI chip play.
CRWV (CoreWeave): about -6% — gives back some of Wednesday's near-25% jump as Nvidia, a key partner, slides.
SONO (Sonos): +13% — quarterly beat on revenue and earnings.
MRCY (Mercury Systems): +13% — strong earnings beat.
MSTR (Strategy): lower — MSCI is removing the stock from its global indexes.
BABA (Alibaba): down more than 6% in Hong Kong as reports tie its access to Nvidia compute to the Nvidia story.

sections.title: Business News
items: Axios reports President Trump authorized a crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia AI chips to China; the curbs are not yet in place.
China urged Washington not to use the Nvidia allegations as grounds for tighter chip export limits, according to Bloomberg.
Alphabet launched a bond sale in Asia, the latest in a run of big tech borrowing to fund AI buildouts.
Exxon is assessing seven areas in Venezuela, Reuters reports.
Oil traders are watching reports that Vice President Vance may hold talks with a senior Iranian official, and Iranian reports of explosions on two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT: weekly jobless claims, plus any Fed speaker comments on a larger December hike.
Nvidia headlines: any board statement on its CEO could swing chip stocks and the Nasdaq.
After the close: Applied Materials results, a read on chip equipment demand; the 10-year yield near 5% is a key level.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Thursday, November twelfth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the dawn patrol, as always, is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog. Give 'em a holler, Gus! Alright, let's check the swell. Conditions are poor this morning, with a choppy break in tech. S and P five hundred futures are down about three tenths of a percent. Nasdaq one hundred futures are off about seven tenths of a percent. Dow futures are just about flat, up a tenth, and small caps are flat too. The ten year Treasury yield sits near four point nine nine percent. Crude is down about half a percent, near eighty six dollars. Gold is off nearly one percent. Bitcoin is down about one percent, near seventy four thousand dollars. The fear gauge, the VIX, is creeping up toward eighteen. Now the gnarly part. Nvidia is down about five and a half percent before the bell. Reports say its board is weighing the future of chief executive Jensen Huang over allegations about his personal conduct. None of it has been confirmed by the company, and traders are paddling over to rivals. A M D is up about four percent, and Broadcom is up more than three percent. CoreWeave is giving back about six percent after its huge run yesterday. Over on the tide chart, Sonos beat on sales and profit, and the stock is up about thirteen percent. Now that's a hang ten move. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Mercury Systems also beat, and it's up about thirteen percent too. After the close, Applied Materials reports, and Cisco is on deck today as well. For wind and weather, weekly jobless claims hit at seven thirty A M Central. Yesterday's inflation report ran hot, so we've got a crowd of Fed speakers today. Traders want to know if a bigger December rate hike is on the table. In beach talk, reports say the White House okayed a crackdown on chips being diverted to China. Sets to watch: jobless claims, any Nvidia board news, and that ten year yield near five percent. Soul surfers, stay stoked and don't let one gnarly set knock you off your board. Got a stock, an E T F or a futures contract on your mind?
